proposed_from.topic: Atom-safe critical inference for rare-arm adaptive experiments. Fix binary-arm finite populations with bounded potential outcomes, logged predictable assignment probabilities, deterministic bounded Lipschitz critical intensity and signed-residual profiles with supplied uniform moduli, and an explicit early quadratic-variation envelope. Construct a computable stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson finite-transfer bound and logged-profile enclosure; use certified profile nets and signed-mark convolution to return confidence intervals with uniform finite-experiment coverage and oracle alpha/radius slack, including atomic laws. Prove that the exact late-ramp pair forces every 95%-honest confidence set to have diameter at least 1/8 with limiting probability at least 0.60710678, while a declared high-hazard subfamily admits robust radius at most 0.442M plus arbitrarily small certification slack. Keep HT distributional limits distinct from all-estimator information bounds. Consumer: Liberali et al.'s GUSTO-1/EUROPA adaptive-randomization analysis, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint profile bridge. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A stopped coupling, Bernoulli-to-Poisson comparison, Riemann-grid error, random-residual mark bound, and deterministic log-enclosure contraction were derived. The transfer chain uses a predictable stopping rule, summed propensity-probability errors, a Le Cam Bernoulli-to-Poisson step, and Lipschitz Riemann control. Campbell/isometry bounds control random residual marks and early quadratic variation. Rational profile nets, interval elementary functions, and deterministic threshold monotonicity make calibration effective rather than existential. A selection-safe monotone-threshold lemma handles calibration from the same propensity log. Directed BigInt convolution on a 16-bin envelope certified the two-sign ramp expectation below 0.037934 at radius 13/32, while the common void event tends to 0.70710678; a full signed-mark tail calculation gives 0.049830 at radius 0.442M on the high-hazard family. Checks covered completed-log conditioning, pathwise selection, early exceptional propensities, finite-activity atoms, quantile discontinuities, zero and signed profiles, finite-n normalization, and legal high-hazard membership. The constant-profile law was identified as generalized Dickman rather than a new obstruction, so the proposed contribution is the uniform finite-transfer and profile-adaptive interval theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently implement and prove the end-to-end logged-profile-net convolution certificate, including stopped-coupling and deterministic-threshold error allocation, uniformly over the declared adaptive class. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact c=a=1/2, delta=1/4 ramp certificate and preserve both the 0.60710678 diameter lower bound and the 0.442M high-hazard radius; any violation stops the calibration route. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The two closest inferential results are LiZhao2026 and WaudbySmithEtAl2024. The gap relative to Li and Zhao is coverage in a declared subset of their adaptive finite-population design framework that violates their Lindeberg route: \(e_{nt}\asymp\bar q(t/n)/t\) yields order-one rare-arm increments and an atomic signed compound-Poisson limit. Relative to Waudby-Smith et al., the advance is not generic validity but profile-specific finite-horizon radius: the completed log is converted into a simultaneous intensity enclosure, and every numerical, coupling, and threshold error is charged explicitly. FreidlingZhaoGao2026 protects exact post-selection randomization tests by conditioning; here completed-log conditioning is invalid for an approximate independent reference, so the new selection-safe move is deterministic threshold domination. ChenEtAl2026 is the closest newly located compound-Poisson HT collision, but its Poisson population size and independent importance draws make the compound-Poisson model exact; it provides neither a predictable adaptive transfer nor a signed finite-population ATE theorem. The all-set late-ramp lower bound is deliberately proved from a shared subprobability measure on the complete observation and is not inferred from the HT law. BarbourXia1999 and BhattacharjeeGoldstein2019 supply approximation and Dickman precedents but do not subsume adaptive signed-mark calibration.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Section 2, Condition 3, Theorem 4, the proof in Supplement S2.3, the vanishing-probability simulation in Section 6.3, and the Discussion. The proof writes AIPW error as a martingale array and invokes variance convergence plus Lindeberg; the first changed step at \(e_{nt}\asymp 1/t\) is to replace the martingale CLT by stopped Bernoulli coupling and marked-Poisson transfer.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct an atom-safe, finite-error confidence interval and pair it with an all-procedure honest-width frontier in the bounded-hazard design-based experiment.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Uniformly couple \(S_n\) to \(Z_{r,\bar q}\) with a computable error budget, certify same-log critical radii over profile nets, prove uniform coverage and oracle slack, and separately prove the exact late-ramp diameter lower bound and high-hazard upper radius.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Li and Zhao's martingale Lindeberg verification fails because a single rare-arm inverse-propensity increment remains order one; stop at envelope violations and couple the remaining predictable Bernoulli draws to independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\bar q(t/n)/t)\) draws.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining adaptive finite-population inference, bounded cumulative hazard, compound-Poisson confidence intervals, signed marks, and logged propensity calibration found LiZhao2026, WaudbySmithEtAl2024, ChoBibautKallus2025, and classical Poisson approximation, but no theorem containing this target-method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from LiZhao2026 because their design-based AIPW theorem already permits vanishing propensities.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their Theorem 4(ii) is Gaussian only under Condition 3, whose Lindeberg term excludes order-one critical increments; their Section 6.3 documents failure as probabilities decay faster, and it supplies neither an atomic critical-law calibration nor an all-set lower bound.
seed_details.burned_reason: The sole field-target proposal angle was fully derived and maximized but graded subfield because its positive procedure remains on a supplied structured profile class and its matching attainment is pair-specific.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Proposition 1 and its conditional-randomization construction, Supplement S2, and the Discussion. Their selection protection conditions on assignments that reproduce the same design choice; the first changed step is to replace exact conditional randomization simulation by simultaneous outward-rounded bounds for an approximate atomic law.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove that a profile-net index chosen from the same completed propensity log can be used for calibration without conditioning on that log as if assignments became independent.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A deterministic monotone-threshold lemma turns simultaneous profile enclosures into selection-safe unconditional coverage and an oracle radius inequality at atoms.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace equality of the conditional randomization kernel after selection by a pathwise inclusion between the selected threshold and the deterministic robust threshold of the true profile.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for selective randomization with compound-Poisson calibration or certified profile nets returned FreidlingZhaoGao2026 and generic martingale methods, but no deterministic atom-safe enclosure theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from selective randomization inference because choosing a profile is just another selection event.
seed_details.rebuttal: The exact conditional randomization law is not available after adaptive-to-Poisson approximation, and conditioning on the completed propensity log does not yield independent assignments; the required proof is a simultaneous deterministic enclosure plus threshold monotonicity argument.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Theorem 1 and its martingale-CLT proof outline, the truncation experiment in Section 4.3, and the Conclusion. The paper explicitly identifies finite-time truncation and confidence-set width as open directions; the first changed step is to compare complete sequential logged experiments through their shared no-rare-assignment submeasure rather than to analyze one A2IPW statistic.
seed_details.opportunity: Determine a non-Gaussian honest-diameter adaptation obstruction over late-ramp laws and contrast it with a high-hazard profile class.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For an exact \(c=a=1/2\), \(\delta=1/4\) pair, every \(95\%\)-honest confidence set has diameter at least \(1/8\) with limiting probability at least \(\sqrt{1/2}-0.1\); a separate certified interval has robust high-hazard radius at most \(0.442M\) plus slack.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace semiparametric influence-function or estimator-width analysis by a common-subprobability argument for the full assignment, propensity, and outcome observation.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent searches found ShekharRamdas2023 for i.i.d. bounded means and HongLeungLi2020 for diverging effective sample size, but no adaptive finite-population void-event information bound.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from a two-point Le Cam bound because the two ramp laws differ only when the rare arm is assigned.
seed_details.rebuttal: The full adaptive propensity log can itself differ across histories, so the shared subprobability measure and legal class membership must be established at experiment level; the exact constant and the separation from an HT limit are not supplied by generic Le Cam prose.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace stationarity-and-exchangeability resampling of patient pools by a fixed-potential-outcome sequential randomization law conditional on the prespecified bridge.

seed_details.rebuttal: Insertion alone does not verify the deterministic profile moduli over all counterfactual histories, and their Gaussian conditions do not cover bounded hazard; the application remains conditional until a bridge contract is established.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Algorithm 1, Theorem 1 and its proof in Appendix D, the Conclusion, and the limitations section. Their optimism argument yields asymptotic type-I control for specified bandit examples; the first changed step is to replace nuisance-biased trajectory simulation by a deterministic enclosure of every admissible signed critical law.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize when simulation-with-optimism and certified Poisson calibration agree and when atoms force divergent thresholds.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Derive an observable frontier in profile uncertainty and atom mass separating asymptotic equivalence of simulated and certified critical values from persistent threshold divergence.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace consistency of simulated nuisance laws with a quantitative Wasserstein-to-ramp bound uniform over the logged profile enclosure.
seed_details.destination_search: No source found an explicit atom-mass and profile-modulus frontier for adaptive simulation calibration.
seed_details.red_team: Routine from weak convergence plus Monte Carlo consistency.
seed_details.rebuttal: Weak convergence does not control discontinuous quantiles at atoms, so equivalence requires a derived smoothing and anti-discontinuity frontier; nevertheless the exact frontier is less directly supported than the selected seed.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction and desiderata, Theorem 1 with its test-martingale proof, fixed-time Corollary 1, and the Summary. Their wealth-process inversion is exact under predictable logging; the first changed step would be to replace a generic terminal boundary with a horizon-indexed compound-Poisson threshold while protecting every stopping time.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct an anytime-valid atom-safe confidence sequence whose terminal widths adapt to the critical intensity profile.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Combine a test-martingale safety layer with profile-specific Poisson terminal calibrations at a deterministic epoch grid.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The marginal critical-law transfer must be made simultaneous over epochs before Ville inversion can protect arbitrary stopping.
seed_details.destination_search: The Waudby-Smith et al. confidence sequences already give validity without bounded importance weights; no result found a sharp bounded-hazard compound-Poisson width guarantee.
seed_details.red_team: Generic confidence sequences already solve validity and any profile calibration is only a tuning improvement.
seed_details.rebuttal: The profile-specific atomic width could be new, but time-uniform protection may erase the proposed gain and the fixed-horizon consumer is more immediate.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the same source sections as for the honest-width seed, especially Section 4.3, where truncation materially changes finite-time width, and the Conclusion's design question.
seed_details.opportunity: Choose an exploration floor that minimizes certified rare-arm interval radius subject to a patient-benefit constraint.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A minimax allocation rule with a KKT or saddle certificate for the tradeoff between cumulative inferior-arm exposure and worst-case design-based radius.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote the truncation level from an inferential tuning choice to the design decision variable and derive a matching lower bound over feasible adaptive rules.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent adaptive-design work optimizes asymptotic variance or regret, but the present substrate does not yet supply a convex criterion for the atomic certified radius.
seed_details.red_team: A standard exploration-floor optimization once a variance formula is available.
seed_details.rebuttal: At bounded hazard the objective is an atomic profile quantile rather than variance, but no credible optimality certificate is yet visible, so the seed is dropped rather than padded.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read Theorem 4, the AIPW covariance discussion, Supplement S2.3, Section 6.3, and the Discussion. Their local efficiency language remains tied to Gaussian normalization; the first changed step is to define a bounded-hazard local experiment before asking for an efficiency bound.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the discontinuity between semiparametric Gaussian efficiency and finite-activity critical experiments.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A local asymptotic experiment showing where influence-function efficiency ceases to order procedures and a compound-Poisson decision bound replaces it.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace quadratic local asymptotic normality by convergence of likelihood ratios on the rare-assignment point process.

seed_details.red_team: Not well posed because fixed finite-population potential outcomes do not by themselves define differentiable local submodels.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds without an added local model, so this seed is dropped rather than assuming the information structure it seeks to derive.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the multiarm setup in Section 2, Theorems 1 and 4, their martingale proofs, and the Discussion. The first changed step would couple several rare-arm indicators to a multivariate marked Poisson process under the simplex constraint.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: A multivariate signed compound-Poisson transfer and simultaneous confidence region for a fixed contrast matrix.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace coordinatewise Bernoulli coupling by a categorical-to-Poisson coupling that preserves mutual exclusivity and cross-arm drift.
seed_details.destination_search: Multivariate Poisson approximation exists, but the extension from the binary kernel risks being a routine vectorization without a new frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Routine binary-to-fixed-\(K\) extension of the selected theorem.
